subject: flamingo
pitch: An elegant flamingo standing tall in shallow water. Candy-pink feathers deepening to coral on the wings, with a flash of black flight feathers at the wing tips, an S-curved neck, a bent beak that is pale pink with a black tip, pale yellow eyes and long rose-coloured legs with knobbly knees and webbed feet.
reasoning:
I'm planning the flamingo model's proportions and scale—roughly 1.4m tall with long legs and neck—and deciding it should stand with feet touching the floor at y=0, possibly with a shallow water surface included.

I'm now working out the skeleton hierarchy: a hip joint at around y=0.85, with legs structured as hip-to-knee-to-ankle chains to capture the characteristic backward-bending leg joint, and the body/neck built off that root.

With 4 points giving 3 spans and 4 names, the final tip joint lands at the last path point parented to the last span joint, which gives me hipL, kneeL, ankleL, and a tip joint correctly. Now I need to check the default "up" orientation the polyline frames assign to each joint.

For the body tubes, I'm deciding to use a sweep over the chain with a radius function that tapers along the leg, rather than stringing together individual rod segments between joint points, since that gives a smoothly skinned tube across the knee corners instead of a jointed rod look.

For the feet, I'm planning a flat webbed foot as an extruded fan shape lying on the ground plane, with toe points spread forward from the ankle and a thin thickness so the bottom sits right at floor level.

Now I'm thinking through the neck geometry — a flamingo's characteristic S-curve built from a few control points rising from the chest, bowing forward and back, then straightening near the head.

I'll build the neck as a chain with three spans, naming the final segment "head" directly so the tip joint doubles as the head attachment point.

For the neck shape, I'm tapering the sweep radius from thicker at the base (~0.05) down to narrower near the top (~0.03), then widening again for a bulkier head sphere.

For the body, I'm thinking of using a lofted ellipsoid shape running from tail to chest, defining a few stations with varying width and height to get that egg-like tilted silhouette, with rounded end caps by default.

I realize the loft needs to bind to a skeletal joint for proper weighting, so I'm planning to create a root "body" joint and pass it explicitly via the bone option in the loft call so the mesh deforms correctly. For the wings, I'm working out the orientation math—picking forward and up vectors to compute the correct normal direction so the wing plume extrudes outward from the body sides rather than through it, positioning each wing at a small x-offset from center.

Now I'm sketching the actual wing outline as a set of 2D points sweeping from the shoulder back toward a tapered tip, with a smaller black subset of points layered slightly further out to represent dark flight feathers at the tip, nudging that layer's offset just enough to avoid z-fighting with the coral base feathers.

For the beak, I'm planning a bent two-mandible shape built from swept curves running forward from the head and then angling downward, tapering the width and height along the sweep so the tip narrows and flattens, with a pale pink base transitioning toward a black tip.

I'll color this using a gradient paint that blends from a soft pink near the base to near-black at the tip, applied directly to the sweep. The lower mandible gets its own jaw joint hinged off the head, positioned slightly below and offset forward, with the hinge axis running along local X so it can open like a real beak.

For the eyes, I'm placing small pale yellow spheres on either side of the head joint with tiny dark pupils, then adding the head itself as a slightly larger pink sphere positioned just above. For the legs, I'm working out joint placement for the hip, backward-bending knee, and ankle so the knobby rose-colored legs bend in the flamingo's characteristic backward-knee way.

I'm weighting the feet extrusion to the toe bone, then adding knobbly knee spheres at the joint locations. For the legs I'm setting up a tapered sweep that's thicker near the hip and narrows toward the toe, using a six-sided radial profile. I'm also considering whether to add extra plume or tail feather details, but deciding to keep those minimal for now.

Now I'm defining the color palette as a gradient from candy pink on the body deepening into coral on the wings, with black flight feather tips, and working out the wing outline coordinates so the wings fold back flat along the body's z-axis.

Still refining wing geometry...

For the body, I'm setting loft stations along the z-axis: a tapered tail, a wider midsection, and a front with its own width/height, acknowledging the flamingo's tilted posture. For the tail, I'm planning a simple flat fan shape extruded with a slight y-tilt, keeping it thin and coral/pink colored.

Now I'm working through the joint hierarchy: establishing a root "body" joint, then making the hips and neck chains children of that body joint via a parent option, with the neck chain starting near the upper torso and continuing upward into the head and beak.

The head joint comes from the tip of the neck chain, and I'm adding a jaw joint beneath it with a forward-pointing direction for the hinge axis. For the beak, I'm using a curved catmull path swept with a radius function to shape the upper beak bone, bending it downward toward the tip rather than using a straight polyline.

For the lower mandible, I'm sweeping a similar catmull path from the jaw joint with a smaller radius, applying a pale pink-to-black gradient paint shared between both beak pieces since the paint works in bind-pose world space. Then I'm adding small pale yellow eye spheres on either side of the head with tiny dark pupil spheres positioned slightly forward, followed by starting the main head sphere geometry.

Now I'm defining the leg chains for each side as a function of a sign value, laying out joint positions for hip, knee, ankle, and toe that trace the flamingo's characteristic bent-leg shape down to the ground, then adding small knee and ankle knob spheres bound to those joints for visual detail.

For the feet, I'm shaping a webbed toe outline using lateral and forward offsets to create a fanned three-toe silhouette, then extruding it with thickness and positioning it at the ankle-to-toe location so the foot sits flat on the ground just forward of the leg.

Now I'm settling on colors: rose for feet matching the legs, pink gradients for the neck and head, and body pink deepening toward coral on the wings.

I'm considering whether to add a shallow water element since the pose implies standing in water, thinking through a thin disc or cylinder near the feet, but worrying its surface height would partially submerge the feet in an odd way — I may need to adjust the foot position or skip the water feature for simplicity.

Still structuring the build function...

Now thinking through the wing extrude calls, making sure the outline points as number arrays match the expected OutlineInput type, and confirming thickness and color are required extrude options.

Setting bone to "body" for wings and tip so they follow the body's movement. For feet, I'm extruding with bone set to the toe joints.

For loft calls, I'm structuring station data as {at, w, h} objects that get interpolated with a catmull curve through their centers. I'm checking that hip and body geometry line up correctly underneath for the legs to attach cleanly.

For the tail, I'm working out the position and orientation vectors so the plane spans correctly, then defining a fan-shaped outline for the tail silhouette with a small thickness.

Now I'm defining the color gradients for different body parts -- pink for the main body, coral for the wings, with each gradient defined by two anchor points and a blend direction so the shading works symmetrically on both sides. I'm also setting up solid colors for the head and legs, and a gradient for the beak that fades toward black at the tip.

For the beak tip, I'm trying to get a soft transition instead of a hard edge, so I'm reaching for a smoothstep-based mix function to blend the pale beak color into black only near the very end -- but I'm running into a naming conflict since there seem to be two different `mix` functions in the SDK (one for colors, one for bone weights) that could clash on import.

Confirming the explicit paint export takes precedence, so I'm settling on mixing a pale pink into near-black starting around z 0.40 for the upper beak and 0.42 for the lower, with yellow eyes and dark pupils, and a cyan water tone for the scene.

For the wing, I'm extruding a feather-shaped outline positioned relative to the body, mapping the outline's local coordinates onto the body's forward/up plane so the wing silhouette fans backward from the shoulder. I'm adding a second, smaller extrusion for the black feather tips, mirrored by the sx sign and nudged slightly outward and thinner than the main wing shape.

I'm extruding a simple fan-shaped outline for the tail using tilted x/y basis vectors anchored to the body, then adding a thin flat cylinder for the water surface beneath the flamingo, fixing the cylinder's top/bottom radii to match for a flat disc.
